newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha's Democrats claim victory in Albania poll.
newsitem.headline: Berisha's Democrats claim victory in Albania poll.

text.p: Albania's ruling Democratic Party on Monday claimed a landslide victory in local elections on Sunday, considered a test for the country's fledgling democracy and closely watched by international observers.

Party leaders told hundreds of jubilant supporters converging at the central Tirana headquarters of President Sali Berisha's Democrats they had won the majority of city halls across the Balkan nation.

"Preliminary data shows the Democratic Party has achieved a landslide victory," party leader Tritan Shehu said according to Albanian state television. "That is the greatest victory for Albania's democracy."
Some 2.2 million Albanians turned out in force to vote in polls largely free of the controversy that marred parliamentary elections five months ago.
According to Shehu, turnout was more than 75 percent. He said the high figure was testimony to "Albanians' will to contribute to the construction of a democratic society."
Namik Dokle, a senior leader of the opposition Socialists, said it was too early to give a forecast for the results and accused the Democrats of a propaganda ploy in doing so now.
Final results of the battle for 64 town councils, 36 district councils and 310 communes were expected early this week.
Western monitors kept a close eye on Sunday's ballot, considered by the United States and the European Union to be a test of the ruling Democrats' commitment to democracy.
"In general, the voting process has gone on normally and there were no worrying problems," said Nestor Thereska, chairman of Albania's Central Elections Commission.
The Council of Europe, which coordinated monitoring of the vote, said it was too early to draw final conclusions but added there had been no reports of serious incidents.
"We have to wait for our people to tell us what they have found. I must say none of our observers has called in to report any dramatic occurrences," said a Council official.

The Council of Europe, coordinating 365 international observers overseeing the vote, said its representatives were present at polling stations to watch the counting. Earlier it praised the level of cooperation it had received.

Most opposition parties, including the Socialists, boycotted the general elections in May and June, alleging vote rigging by Berisha's Democrats -- charges supported by some internatonal observers. The Democrats claimed a landslide victory in that vote.

On Sunday, the Democratic Party and the Socialists denounced each other for alleged irregularities, especially in rural areas and smaller towns, but neither party presented any significant complaints.
In the last local polls in July 1992, the Socialists won more town halls than the Democrats but the governing party took all the big cities, including Tirana.
